fr.elements: Main Residence; Access Drive; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Detached Structure
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Open Terrain; Dense Vegetation
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with posts or reflective delineators on both sides to define the entry point, especially in low-light or smoky conditions.
• Trim trees and shrubs along the driveway to maintain clearance for emergency vehicles along the full length of the drive.
• Keep the driveway surface clear of parked vehicles, equipment, or debris so emergency vehicles can travel its full length without obstruction.
• Identify and maintain a turnaround area near the main residence so fire and emergency vehicles can reverse direction without backing the full length of the driveway.
• Post the address number visibly at or near the detached structure if it sits at a distance from the main residence, so responders can identify it as a separate building on the property.
• Thin dense vegetation along the driveway edges so responders on foot can move alongside vehicles if needed.
• Keep a clear path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between the two buildings without pushing through overgrown areas.
• If a gate controls driveway access, equip it with a Knox Box or responder-compatible lock so emergency crews are not delayed at the entrance.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Open Terrain; Scattered Shrubs; Brush Area; Scattered Shrubs; Ground Vegetation; Single Access Route; Vegetation Along Driveway; Open Green Space; Scattered Trees; Brush Area; Limited Turnaround Area
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs that are growing close to the house on all sides.
• Remove brush from the area immediately surrounding the structure.
• Thin scattered trees near the house to increase open space between them and the structure.
• Clear ground vegetation within the area directly around the house.
• Cut back shrubs and brush growing along both sides of the driveway.
• Trim any tree branches that hang over or reach across the driveway.
• Keep the driveway surface clear so vehicles can move through without obstruction.
• Create a wider cleared area near the end of the driveway so vehicles can turn around.
• Remove or cut back brush at any curves or narrow points along the driveway where visibility is limited.
• Separate shrub groupings near the house so there are open gaps between them and the structure.
• Cut back brush at the edges of the open green space where it meets the structure or driveway.
